rationale: Evidence from iteration 7 (score 931.4, best so far): all 60 development trials finished (oval 20/20, s-bend 20/20, slalom 20/20). Mean times are 2.16 s (oval), 2.37 s (s-bend) and 2.75 s (slalom), and rms_error is 0.006 to 0.014 m. The score is now limited by three small terms: line_loss_events of 1.0 on every track (about 15 points each), completion time (about 17 points lost on the oval and about 5 on the slalom), and a small rms term. Off-track exits, which cost about 500 points each, have been eliminated on the development tracks, so there is some margin to trade for speed. Iteration 7's kd 1.2 and mass 0.5 kg kept oscillation low (oval 0.21), so the steering is not jittering. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.0 to 1.1. Time is worth up to 60 points, and a 10 percent speed increase should cut the oval time by about 0.15 s and the slalom time by about 0.2 s, gaining roughly 3 to 4 points per track. The slalom would still finish comfortably within 3 s. (2) All other values are unchanged (sensors at y=0.08 across +/-0.045 m, weights, kp 2.0, ki 0.05, kd 1.2, mass 0.5, line_loss last_direction), so the effect of speed alone can be read. Expected result: score about 935 to 940, with completion times falling and line_loss_events and off-track exits staying at zero to one per run. Risk: a faster run may lose the line more often on the tightest slalom bends, which would cost about 15 points per event and could cause an off-track exit (about 500 points). Hypotheses: H10, the single line-loss event per run happens at a fixed point (likely the start or the finish, since it appears on every track at a similar rate), not on the tightest bends, so it is not affected by speed. H11, the time saving from base_speed is larger than the extra loss risk on the development tracks. Measurements wanted next: completion_time on all tracks to confirm the time saving; line_loss_events and max_error on the slalom to test H10 and check for loss from speed; completion and progress on the slalom to rule out off-track exits; and steering_oscillation to confirm kd 1.2 is still not causing jitter at the higher speed.
